thread:
nina: Heads-up: SAST started failing on a bunch of low-risk PRs this morning. Noise comes from test fixtures that include a PEM blob used only for local dev. The scanner flags it as 'possible private key' and blocks merges. We need a triage + long-term fix.

ravi: Seen it. The pipeline job that extracts artifacts for the SAST run is configured to pull `ci-artifacts/test-fixtures/*.pem`. Those are actually encrypted at rest with a KMS key, but the pipeline runner doesn't have kms:Decrypt on the test-key CMK, so we get partial failures and inconsistent scan results.

lee: From QA: most of these are false positives — the PEMs are self-signed dev certs. They break the gating because the scanner treats any key-like blob as P0. Can we tweak the scanner rules to lower severity for `self-signed` heuristics, or better, mark the fixtures path as internal?

maria: Two problems here: (1) perms gaps (pipeline can't decrypt test keys) and (2) noisy rules + lack of repo-level suppression metadata. We should avoid ad-hoc exemptions in Slack. Proposals below.

nina: Proposals (short-term -> long-term):
1) Short-term hotfix: update CI service account `ci-runner@redwood-ci.iam.gserviceaccount.com` with key-level kms:Decrypt for the test-key so scans run deterministically. Scope to the single key.
2) Add a repo-level scanner suppression file `security/scan-suppressions.yaml` that lists known test fixture paths + signature and a short rationale. Scanner will consult this file during CI and not block on those matches (but still record findings in the dashboard).
3) Medium: move dev-only PEMs into a separate encrypted bucket `gs://redwood-dev-fixtures` with a tighter IAM boundary and lifecycle policy so they never get shipped in PR artifacts. CI can fetch them when needed with explicit grants.
4) Long-term: update SAST ruleset to include a fingerprint for dev certs (self-signed -> severity=info) and add a PR label `sast-allowed-fixture` that requires a manual security ack before the scanner exception becomes a permanent suppression.

ravi: I'm okay adding the key-level binding for the CI runner for now. Will do the gcloud one-off and then follow up with a Terraform change to track it. Command I plan to run: 
```
gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding projects/redwood-ci/locations/global/keyRings/test-keys/cryptoKeys/test-key \
  --member=serviceAccount:ci-runner@redwood-ci.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
  --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter
```
I'll also attach the AdminActivity audit link when done.

lee: For the suppression file: I'll draft `security/scan-suppressions.yaml` with entries like: 
```
- path: "ci-artifacts/test-fixtures/*.pem"
  reason: "dev self-signed certs used by local integration tests"
  expires: "2026-07-01"
  owner: "qa@redwood.com"
```
Scanner will read this during run and downgrade findings matching the path to INFO. We still surface them in the UI.

maria: A few guardrails:
- Do not allow permanent suppressions without a security review (SEC-491).
- All IAM changes must be terraform-managed within 72 hours; one-off gcloud binds are allowed as emergency hotfix but must be converted to TF and peer-reviewed.
- Enable AdminActivity audit logs for projects where CI modifies KMS bindings and add an alert on IAM policy changes that affect `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter`.

nina: Also, scanner false-positive mitigation: add a pre-merge SAST dry-run check in dev's pre-commit or CI (non-blocking) so authors see scanner noise locally: 
```
# suggested local run
./tools/sast-runner --paths ci-artifacts/test-fixtures --config .sast-config.yaml
```
If devs see the false positives locally they can add an entry to the suppression draft PR describing why.

ravi: I'll push the TF PR for the KMS binding this afternoon and tag @maria + @nina for review. For the hotfix I'll run the gcloud now and paste the audit link here.

maria: nit: scope the TF binding to the principal `serviceAccount:ci-runner@redwood-ci.iam.gserviceaccount.com` and the specific key resource path. Also add a comment in the TF describing why this is needed (link to SEC ticket).

security-bot: Automated note: creating SEC-491 to track root cause + remediation steps. Also will add an IAM-change watch for `projects/redwood-ci` and send weekly summary to #eng-security.

lee: One more: for build reproducibility, consider stripping test fixtures from the PR artifact bundle by default and requiring explicit inclusion via an opt-in flag in CI. This reduces accidental leakage and reduces scan noise.

nina: Action items: 
- ravi: run one-off gcloud binding (hotfix) and open TF PR to codify (owner)
- lee: add initial `security/scan-suppressions.yaml` draft and a CI hook to load it (owner)
- maria: enable AdminActivity audit alerts and review IAM-watch rules (owner)
- nina: write short runbook SEC-491 describing: how to triage SAST false positives, how to emergency-grant key decrypt rights, and how to convert one-off binds to TF.

ravi: hotfix applied. AdminActivity entry: https://console.cloud.google.com/logs/query;resource=project/redwood-ci;cursor=abcd1234 (added roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter to ci-runner). Opening TF PR: https://git.redwood.com/infra/terraform/pulls/452 (WIP).

maria: Verified audit log shows AdminActivity. Thank you. Once TF PR merges, we should have a post-deploy check to ensure the binding is present and matches TF state.

nina: Great work. We'll follow up with SEC-491 postmortem to confirm the long-term mitigations (move fixtures, suppression lifecycle, rule tuning). Closing thread for now but leave suppression PR open for review. :white_check_mark:
